newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE spot white sugar turns lower as NY weakens.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE spot white sugar turns lower as NY weakens.

text.p: Activity picked up on London's white sugar futures market on Wednesday afternoon as a bearish performance on the New York market dampened sentiment on the whites, traders said.
May raws failed to show any inclination to revisit the 11.00 cents/lb level and drifted lower, sparking selling of the equivalent May whites contract and limited arbitrage activity.
Hedge selling throughout the day against the European Union's weekly tender for sugar export licences also pressured May lower, although bargain hunters were noted at the lower levels.
"There's also good scale-down buying and the premium has widened out a bit," said one trader, noting that the May/May premium was trading at around $67.50, around $1.00 wider than Tuesday's close.
At 1615 GMT May stood $1.10 lower at $305.70 and dominated the overall volume of 949 lots. August was unchanged at $305.20.
Activity was expected to be on the quiet side for the remainder of the session.
"This is the best day we've had for a while...but we're just sitting here quietly and it doesn't look like there'll be much more action," the trader said.
The Paris market showed a relatively healthy volume, largely on account of the EU tender, market sources said.
May was down 90 cents at $305.80 and August down 20 cents at $305.00. Matif volume was 624 lots.
